findings.finding: F1 — legion/INFRA-117 already exists on GitHub at main's head and nothing says how the issue branch comes to sit on envoy-infra-integration; a backwards bookmark move is the only shape that keeps handoff_complete working, and the rewrite guard was not written for it.
findings.answer: Plan section 3 (D1) decides it: the planner repoints legion/INFRA-117 onto envoy-infra-integration@origin with `jj bookmark set ... --allow-backwards` and builds the plan handoff there. Evidence that nothing is lost: `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/compare/main...legion/INFRA-117` returns status identical, ahead_by 0, behind_by 0, so the branch carries no work. The rewrite guard does not apply because no commit is rewritten, rebased or re-parented — only a branch ref moves. Precedent: PR #2089 (legion/INFRA-62, base envoy-infra-integration, merged 2026-10-21) has `93eb442bd plan: record handoff` as its first commit with parent ba3f6b7e, that day's integration-branch head, so that issue's planner made the same move. The plan gives the post-push machine check (compare envoy-infra-integration...legion/INFRA-117) and records the base SHA on the PR body's Chain line. The decision is reported to the architect with this completion.

findings.finding: F2 — 'adopt those commits, do not rewrite the change' has several readings, and the adopted commit b096a8708 is authored and committed by a human identity, which collides with Legion's commit-identity rules.
findings.answer: Plan section 2 (D2) picks the reading and makes it checkable: keep b096a8708's tree byte for byte, adopted with `jj duplicate b096a8708 -d <tip>` (jj 0.45.1 in the pane supports -d), falling back to `jj new` plus `jj restore --from b096a8708 <the twelve paths>`; either way `jj diff --from b096a8708 --to <adopted commit> --git` must print nothing, run once at the adoption commit before the pull request opens. The commit message credits the source. The plan states that the adopted commit carries a human author by design so no role reads it as tampering, and replaces the identity check's revset with the base's, read through `gh api ... --jq '.name | @json'` so the branch name is never typed into revset source.

findings.finding: F3 — every proof surface the spec names needs Docker, which this pod does not have: testnats runs every server through testcontainers, and the new adhoc_topic_test.go takes testnats too.
findings.answer: Plan section 5 (D4) names two real surfaces instead of skipping the proof. S1 is the repository's own natslive harness run in CI — job envoy-infra-go, step 'Live tests of envoy-infra against nats-server (natslive)', `go test -tags natslive ./core/ ./seed/`, which is literally the surface the spec names, recorded by run id and head SHA; both workflows do run on a pull request to this base (pull_request triggers with packages/envoy/** and no branches filter). S2 is an in-pod live rig, measured feasible today: `go install github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2` works from the pod (v2.11.4 installed in 70 s), `go build ./cmd/listener` takes 18 s, and both controls were reproduced against a real nats-server — the pre-change grant logged `Publish Violation - User "listener", Subject "notifications.lxspec.probe.all"` with a 2.002 s subscriber timeout, and `notifications.>` delivered in 0.002 s. The rig renders its authorization from the branch's own core.ListenerPermissions, never a hand-typed grant, and is deleted before the phase completes. The plan also records which local gates run without Docker (`go test ./core/`, `go test ./gcp/ -skip DataDisk`) and that `go test ./...` in infra fails only on data-disk tests needing mkfs.ext4, which this pod lacks.

findings.finding: F4 — the production check after the close can never observe this merge, and the spec does not say what the look should report.
findings.answer: Plan section 10 (D9) decides it: the first look reports verdict pending, and its summary and the pull request's Production: line name the merge commit, say the hub cannot carry it until INFRA-118 moves the deployment repository's two envoy-infra-commit pins, and cite .github/workflows/release-envoy-infra.yaml's `push: branches: [main]` trigger as the evidence that merging here publishes nothing. The implementer also reports to the architect that no automatic wake exists for this check, so it will sit to its bound. Listed as risk R2 and published to the architect with this completion.

findings.finding: F5 — the base has no ruleset, so no CI result and no review can stop the merge, and the issue names no verdict of its own.
findings.answer: Plan section 6 (D5) names the verdict the roles enforce by hand, since the daemon will not: lint, typecheck, test, pr-title, build, changes, envoy-go, envoy-infra-go, envoy-go-race, envoy-smoke, envoy-e2e-local and dispatch-memory must all be success at the CI head before the reviewer approves, re-read by the merger at the READY head, with the exact `gh api .../check-runs` command. The baseline for a job red for unrelated reasons is the same read at #2089's merged head c00fcb28, which gives `failure dispatch` and success for every other job; a red matching that baseline goes on the Not proven / risk line, and any other red is fixed in this pull request. Whether this branch should have a human in the merge loop (projects.INFRA.merge.by_hand, or a ruleset) is outside the issue's reach and is risk R1, published to the architect.

findings.finding: F6 — the adopted change omits the ten documentation and client-contract files the main-line fix carries, and nothing says whether that is deliberate.
findings.answer: Plan section 4 (D3) says it explicitly: the pull request's file set is exactly the twelve files of #2102, and names the ten omitted files. The reasons are recorded — the spec's deliverable names three code behaviours and no documentation; this branch exists only to render the hub's permissions while its skills, TypeScript client and changelog ship from main; and every file edited on both lines is another conflict for INFRA-120's merge, which already left 28 files conflicting in the trial merge INFRA-113's spec records. packages/envoy/infra/README.md stays because it is in the adopted commit and documents the plugin this branch builds. The reviewer checks the set with `gh pr view <n> --json files`.

findings.finding: F7 — equivalence with what INFRA-113 finally lands on main is asserted against #2101, which is not necessarily what will merge, and nobody owns re-syncing it.
findings.answer: Plan section 8 (D6) sets the ordering and the criterion. Ordering: parallel, because the human ruled out gating this on the main-line merge. Criterion: the four fix hunks — usesCoreTransport, streamCaptures, the ListenerPermissions publish list and the api.go prefix refusal — not the file lists, which cannot match across a 290/208 divergence. The implementer re-compares against whatever head INFRA-113 then carries and records the result; the reviewer re-compares at review time; a difference is published to the INFRA-113 architect rather than resolved by a worker; and a change forced after this merges is new work the architect owns (risk R3).

findings.finding: F8 — the caller census behind the new 400 refusal was taken on main, not on this branch, which carries code main does not.
findings.answer: Plan section 7 (D7) puts the census in scope as implementer work: repeat it on the base tree, record every caller of the listener's publish endpoint and of the client's publish with the topic each names, in the pull request body and in implement.json. A caller found only on this branch that publishes outside notifications. is a finding for the architect before the refusal ships, not a worker's decision.

findings.finding: F9 — 'grants the hub listener user notifications.>' understates the change: ListenerPermissions is what HostPermissions and DispatchPermissions build on, so three rendered users widen.
findings.answer: Plan section 1 records it as a measured scope note: all three rendered users — example-host-a, example-dispatch and example-hub — change in the adopted cloud-config goldens, and the acceptance is read as all three. The plan narrows nothing. The wording of the spec's acceptance line is the architect's to change; it is published with this completion.

findings.finding: F10 — streamCaptures judges capture from the subjects the running binary compiled, and on the hub the plugin (this branch) and the listener (an image) come from different builds, with this branch 208 commits behind main.
findings.answer: Recorded as risk R4 in plan section 12 and required on the pull request's Not proven / risk line. No new work here: INFRA-113's approved spec already rules that the new grant and the new listener image ship together, image first if one must lead, and that is INFRA-118's scope. Published to the architect so INFRA-118 carries it.

findings.finding: F11 — closing #2102 is unassigned work with a repository rule attached (no gh issue writes, and every GitHub comment needs the Legion footer).
findings.answer: Plan section 9 (D8) assigns it to the implementer, immediately after gh pr create succeeds, with the exact commands: `gh pr comment 2102` carrying the Legion session footer, then `gh pr close 2102` — both pull-request writes, which the worker rules allow. The branch fix/envoy-adhoc-topics-integration is left in place, since it is not this issue's branch.

findings.finding: Unsupported-claim check — the gap analyst could read neither spec (no Dispatch access in its session) and had no shell, so it could not re-measure the branch protection, the Docker absence, the in-pod nats-server controls or the #2089 precedent; it also found the brief's claim that legion/INFRA-117@origin does not exist to be false.
findings.answer: Every measurement it could not repeat was taken in this session and is cited in the plan with its command: rules/branches/envoy-infra-integration returning [], `which docker` finding nothing, the two in-pod nats-server controls, `go build ./cmd/listener` at 18 s, `go test ./core/` and `go test ./gcp/ -skip DataDisk` passing, and #2089's head check-runs. The false claim is corrected in the plan: legion/INFRA-117 does exist on GitHub at main's head, which is what plan section 3 is written around. The deployment repository's two pins remain unverifiable from this repository by design (check-private-names.sh), so the plan treats them as the issue author's word and assigns nothing to them.

R2 — the production check cannot pass until INFRA-118 deploys; the first look reports pending and no automatic wake exists.
R3 — a change INFRA-113's review forces after this merges has no owner.
R4 — streamCaptures judges capture from the running binary's compiled subjects, so the branch's grant and the listener image must ship together (INFRA-118).
R5 — the base may move under the pull request; the daemon returns the issue to implementing and the documented forward merge applies, with base read from the pull request.
R6 — the dispatch CI job is red on this branch line at the baseline head.
